title: Honey Garlic Wings
subtitle: Fried wings in a sticky sweet-and-savoury glaze
excerpt: Honey garlic wings are fried crisp then tossed in a thick glaze of honey, garlic, soy sauce, and butter. The glaze caramelises slightly on the hot wings to give a sticky, shiny coat. They're sweet, garlicky, and considerably easier to eat than buffalo wings.
sourceNotes: Honey garlic wings are a popular American variation on buffalo wings, developed from the tradition of glazing fried wings in sweet-savoury sauces.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The glaze can be made up to three days ahead.

content.text: Honey garlic wings are fried twice for crispness, then tossed in a glaze of honey, soy sauce, garlic, and butter. The glaze is thick enough to cling without coating them completely: each wing should be shiny rather than sodden. They're sweet and savoury in the way that makes people eat more than they intended.

items.prepNote: tips removed, split at the joint

content.text: Fry the wings in two stages

Pat {{chicken-wings}} very dry. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}}. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} in a large deep pot to 180°C. Fry the wings in batches for eight to ten minutes until cooked through and lightly golden. Remove to a rack.
Increase the oil to 190°C. Fry the wings in batches for three to four minutes more until deeply golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add {{garlic}} and cook for one minute until fragrant. Add {{honey}}, {{soy-sauce-light}}, {{cider-vinegar}}, and {{chilli-flakes}} if using. Stir over medium heat for two to three minutes until the glaze is slightly reduced and coats the back of a spoon.
Transfer the hot wings to a large bowl. Pour the glaze over and toss until every wing is coated. Scatter with {{spring-onion}} if using and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The glaze is too sweet and cloying
items.cause: Honey dominates without enough salt or acid to balance.
items.fix: Add a little more soy sauce and another teaspoon of cider vinegar. The glaze should taste balanced when you dip a spoon in: sweet, salty, and slightly sharp.

items.symptom: The glaze hardens and sticks the wings together
items.cause: Glaze reduced too far, or cooled before tossing.
items.fix: Toss the wings in the glaze immediately while both are hot. If the glaze has thickened too much, thin with a tablespoon of water and reheat before tossing.

items.symptom: The garlic is bitter and sharp
items.cause: Cooked too long over too high a heat.
items.fix: Cook the garlic for no more than a minute over medium heat. It should smell fragrant and look just barely golden, not brown.

items.symptom: Wings are not crispy after two fries
items.cause: Too much moisture in the wings before frying.
items.fix: Dry the wings thoroughly. For extra crispness, dust with a tablespoon of cornflour before the first fry.

content.text: Honey garlic wings are a popular alternative to buffalo wings: same technique, sweeter profile. The honey, garlic, and soy combination has Asian-American roots, but the flavour is now a fixed part of American party food. Serve with rice as a main, or as a snack with plenty of napkins.
